Competing mechanistic protein-load caveat: daytime mixed/animal protein redistribution trial (n=18/21 PD fluctuators) showed balanced daytime protein lengthened daily OFF time (271 vs 164 min, p<0.0001). Marked unusable for cooked edamame exposure because it did not test soy or legumes, yet flags that a full culinary cup of cooked shelled edamame (~18.5 g protein, >4x Nagashima's ~4 g) could introduce LNAA competition if co-ingested with levodopa.
Systematic review (PMC8634393) rating Nagashima 2016 Adjusted Low RoB while emphasizing that soybean ON-time prolongation (270 vs 150 min, p=0.028) requires larger trial confirmation.

Human dual-isotope tracer study showing plant legume proteins have significantly lower true ileal LNAA (tryptophan) digestibility (67.6-74.5%) than whole egg/meat/milk (89.7-95.9%, p<0.05), consistent with slower legume postprandial aminoacidemia (Yimam 2025).

Direct PD crossover (n=7 with wearing-off; 1-wk washout) comparing LD/CD (100/10 mg) + 11 g ground mature Glycine max soybeans (~4 g protein) vs LD/CD alone: prolonged acute self-rated ON-period by 80% (270 vs 150 min, p=0.028) and reduced covariate-adjusted 3-OMD (317.0 vs 374.6 ng/mL, p=0.03), though unadjusted levodopa AUC did not differ significantly. Exposure fit is remote (11 g ground mature soybean vs culinary cooked edamame supplying ~18.5 g protein/cup) and outcome fit is partial (3-h acute ON window vs 24-h daily off time).
